# Live settings (generated reference)

<!-- generated by scripts/gen_docs.py from ait/config/settings.py, config.yaml and config_research.yaml; edit the code, not this file -->

Every setting of the live bot and the supervisor, and the sections research shares (`ml`, `regime`, `meta_label`, `exit`, `options`, ...). Research-only settings (`backtest`, `parity`) are in [SETTINGS_RESEARCH.md](SETTINGS_RESEARCH.md). The *Shipped* column is what `config.yaml` sets; a key it does not list runs at the schema default. Explanations and the rules that link settings: [GUIDE.md](../GUIDE.md#13-configuration-system) and [MODELS.md](../MODELS.md). Secrets come only from `.env` and are never shown here.

374 settings; 0 have no description in the schema yet (shown as `-`).

## Trading universe, mode and cadence (`trading`)

| Setting | Type | Allowed range | Default | Shipped | Listed in | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `trading.mode` | `Literal['paper', 'live']` | - | paper | paper | config.yaml | Paper or live trading. |
| `trading.universe` | `list[str]` | - | [SPY, QQQ, AAPL] | [SPY, QQQ, IWM] | config.yaml | Symbols the bot scans for entries. |
| `trading.scan_interval_seconds` | `int` | 30 - 3600 | 300 | 300 | config.yaml | Seconds between entry scans, counted from when the previous scan finishes. |
| `trading.max_daily_trades` | `int` | 1 - 50 | 5 | 12 | config.yaml | Upper bound on new positions opened per day; the time-of-day trade budget (first hour, midday, rest of the session) is bounded by it. |
| `trading.trading_hours_only` | `bool` | - | true | true | config.yaml | Not read by any code: regular trading hours are enforced unconditionally by the scheduler and by the executor (the executor override is the environment variable AIT_ALLOW_AFTER_HOURS=1). |
| `trading.no_new_entries_minutes_before_close` | `int` | 0 - 120 | 15 | 15 | config.yaml | No new entries inside this many minutes of the session close. |
| `trading.first_hour_end_et` | `str` | - | 10:30 | 10:30 | config.yaml | End of the 'first hour' (ET). |
| `trading.midday_end_et` | `str` | - | 14:00 | 14:00 | config.yaml | End of the mid-day window (ET). |
| `trading.first_hour_trade_budget` | `int` | 1 - 50 | 2 | 2 | config.yaml | Cumulative trade ceiling while before first_hour_end_et (still capped by max_daily_trades). |
| `trading.midday_trade_budget` | `int` | 1 - 50 | 4 | 4 | config.yaml | Cumulative trade ceiling between first_hour_end_et and midday_end_et (still capped by max_daily_trades). |
| `trading.first_hour_min_confidence` | `float` | 0.5 - 0.99 | 0.85 | 0.85 | config.yaml | Confidence a DIRECTIONAL signal needs before first_hour_end_et (neutral/range-gated structures such as iron condors are exempt). |

## Account and capital (`account`)

| Setting | Type | Allowed range | Default | Shipped | Listed in | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `account.pdt_protection` | `bool` | - | true | true | config.yaml | Enables the pattern-day-trader guard; it applies only together with pdt_account_under_25k. |
| `account.pdt_account_under_25k` | `bool` | - | true | false | config.yaml | True when the funded account is a margin account under $25,000, so the pattern-day-trader guard applies. |
| `account.capital` | `float` | 1000.0 - 10000000.0 | 5000.0 | 5000 | config.yaml | THE one capital number. |
| `account.simulate_live_capital` | `bool` | - | true | true | config.yaml | When true, broker/account.py scales every broker balance down to `capital` so the WHOLE live risk stack sizes as that small account while the real paper balance sits underneath. |
| `account.capital_tier_small_min` | `float` | 0.0 - .. | 2000.0 | 2000 | config.yaml | NLV at/above which the SMALL capital tier starts (below it: MICRO). |
| `account.capital_tier_medium_min` | `float` | 0.0 - .. | 5000.0 | 5000 | config.yaml | NLV at/above which the MEDIUM tier starts. |
| `account.capital_tier_large_min` | `float` | 0.0 - .. | 25000.0 | 25000 | config.yaml | NLV at/above which the LARGE tier starts. |

## Position limits and order lifecycle (`positions`)

| Setting | Type | Allowed range | Default | Shipped | Listed in | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `positions.max_open_positions` | `int` | 1 - 20 | 5 | 10 | config.yaml | Maximum number of positions open at once (the risk manager's position-count gate; the research pool applies the same cap). |
| `positions.max_position_pct` | `float` | 0.01 - 0.3 | 0.2 | 0.2 | config.yaml | The position sizer's hard per-position cap, fraction of NLV (a defined-risk structure's max loss per contract must fit). |
| `positions.max_portfolio_delta` | `float` | 0.05 - 1.0 | 0.3 | 0.3 | config.yaml | Net portfolio delta limit as a fraction of account value. |
| `positions.max_portfolio_risk_pct` | `float` | 0.005 - 0.5 | 0.2 | 0.2 | config.yaml | Aggregate capital at risk across all open positions, as a fraction of net liquidation. |
| `positions.entry_ladder_start` | `float` | 0.0 - 1.0 | 0.25 | 0.25 | config.yaml | Config home for AIT_ENTRY_LADDER_START — the fraction of the way from mid to the marketable price at which a combo entry ladder starts. |
| `positions.entry_order_timeout_seconds` | `int` | 30 - 3600 | 240 | 240 | config.yaml | Config home for AIT_ENTRY_ORDER_TIMEOUT — how long an entry order may work before it is cancelled. |
| `positions.max_contracts_per_trade` | `int` | 1 - 100 | 10 | 1 | config.yaml | Hard cap on contracts per trade. |
| `positions.partial_fill_cancel_seconds` | `float` | 5.0 - 300.0 | 30.0 | 30 | config.yaml | An entry order that is only PARTIALLY filled has its unfilled remainder cancelled once it has been working this long, so the position is not left with orphaned legs riding stale prices. |
| `positions.absent_order_grace_seconds` | `float` | 10.0 - 120.0 | 30.0 | 30 | config.yaml | An ENTRY order that is absent from the broker trade list is treated as still pending (not cancelled) while younger than this. |
| `positions.entry_ladder_step_seconds` | `float` | 30.0 - 300.0 | 45.0 | 45 | config.yaml | An unfilled entry combo's limit price steps toward marketable every this many seconds (steps at 0.25 / 0.60 / 1.00 of the offset). |

## Position sizing (`position_sizing`)

| Setting | Type | Allowed range | Default | Shipped | Listed in | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `position_sizing.confidence_size_floor` | `float` | 0.05 - 1.0 | 0.3 | 0.3 | config.yaml | Lowest confidence multiplier (the confidence curve runs 0.5 at risk.min_confidence to 1.0 at confidence 1.0 and is clamped to [this, 1.0]). |
| `position_sizing.iv_full_size_max` | `float` | 0.01 - 2.0 | 0.2 | 0.2 | config.yaml | Implied vol at/below which volatility_adjustment is 1.0. |
| `position_sizing.iv_floor_size_min` | `float` | 0.02 - 3.0 | 0.6 | 0.6 | config.yaml | Implied vol at/above which volatility_adjustment bottoms out at iv_floor_size_factor. |
| `position_sizing.iv_floor_size_factor` | `float` | 0.05 - 1.0 | 0.5 | 0.5 | config.yaml | The volatility multiplier at/above iv_floor_size_min. |
| `position_sizing.iv_rank_adj_min` | `float` | 0.1 - 1.0 | 0.8 | 0.8 | config.yaml | IV-rank multiplier floor: a SELLING strategy at IV rank 0 (or a BUYING one at rank 100) is sized at this factor. |
| `position_sizing.iv_rank_adj_max` | `float` | 1.0 - 3.0 | 1.2 | 1.2 | config.yaml | IV-rank multiplier ceiling: a SELLING strategy at IV rank 100 (or a BUYING one at rank 0) is sized at this factor. |
| `position_sizing.drawdown_tiers` | `list[list[float]]` | - | [[3, 0.5], [5, 0.25]] | [[3, 0.5], [5, 0.25]] | config.yaml | [consecutive_losing_days, size_factor] pairs, ascending by days; the highest threshold met wins (0 losing days or below the first row = 1.0). |
| `position_sizing.vix_size_tiers` | `list[list[float]]` | - | [[25, 0.75], [30, 0.5]] | [[25, 0.75], [30, 0.5]] | config.yaml | [vix_at_or_above, size_factor] pairs, ascending by VIX; the highest threshold met wins (below the first row = 1.0). |
| `position_sizing.strategy_risk` | `dict[str, float]` | - | {long_call: 1.0, long_put: 1.0, covered_call: 0.5, cash_secured_put: 0.5, bull_call_spread: 0.6, bear_put_spread: 0.6, iron_condor: 0.4, long_straddle: 1.2, short_strangle: 0.8, calendar_spread: 0.7, event_straddle: 0.7} | {long_call: 1.0, long_put: 1.0, covered_call: 0.5, cash_secured_put: 0.5, bull_call_spread: 0.6, bear_put_spread: 0.6, iron_condor: 0.4, long_straddle: 1.2, short_strangle: 0.8, calendar_spread: 0.7, event_straddle: 0.7} | config.yaml | Per-strategy fraction of the position budget. |

## Risk limits (`risk`)

| Setting | Type | Allowed range | Default | Shipped | Listed in | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `risk.max_daily_loss_pct` | `float` | 0.005 - 0.2 | 0.2 | 0.2 | config.yaml | Daily loss breaker, fraction of NLV (realised AND mark-to-market trips; entries only, exits keep running). 0.02 -> 0.045 at the $5k account (breaker $225 vs the $3-wide condor's $201-212 max loss on real chains); the startup self-test's rule is breaker >= breaker_to_max_loss_ratio x the largest max loss the builder emits. |
| `risk.breaker_to_max_loss_ratio` | `float` | 0.5 - 3.0 | 1.0 | 1.0 | config.yaml | The startup coherence check (orchestrator A2) alerts when the daily-loss breaker is below this multiple of the LARGEST single max loss the real condor builder emits. |
| `risk.max_consecutive_losses` | `int` | 1 - 10 | 3 | 3 | config.yaml | Consecutive losing closes that trip the circuit breaker. |
| `risk.pause_minutes_after_losses` | `int` | 5 - 120 | 30 | 30 | config.yaml | Minutes new entries stay paused after the consecutive-losses trip. |
| `risk.max_api_failures` | `int` | 2 - 20 | 5 | 5 | config.yaml | Broker API failures within 10 minutes that trip the circuit breaker (10-minute pause). |
| `risk.min_confidence` | `float` | 0.5 - 0.95 | 0.65 | 0.5 | config.yaml | Minimum model confidence for an entry. |
| `risk.pre_event_blackout_days` | `int` | 0 - 7 | 1 | 1 | config.yaml | Block NEW credit entries within N calendar days of a macro event (NFP/CPI/PCE). |
| `risk.max_position_risk_pct` | `float` | 0.005 - 0.25 | 0.2 | 0.2 | config.yaml | Maximum loss of one trade as a fraction of net liquidation, and the budget the condor builder is handed to size the wings. |
| `risk.max_correlation` | `float` | 0.3 - 0.99 | 0.75 | 0.75 | config.yaml | Correlation above which two symbols count as the same bet. |
| `risk.max_correlated_positions` | `int` | 1 - 8 | 2 | 2 | config.yaml | Max simultaneous positions within one correlated cluster (SPY/QQQ/IWM/DIA correlate ~0.95). |
| `risk.post_stop_cluster_cooldown_minutes` | `int` | 0 - 1440 | 120 | 120 | config.yaml | Post-stop re-entry cooldown for CLUSTER SIBLINGS of a stopped-out symbol. |
| `risk.max_credit_positions` | `int` | 1 - 20 | 6 | 6 | config.yaml | Max simultaneous short-premium (credit) positions. |
| `risk.credit_cap_vix_tiers` | `list[list[float]]` | - | [[20.0, 6], [25.0, 4], [999.0, 2]] | [[20.0, 6], [25.0, 4], [999.0, 2]] | config.yaml | VIX-tiered credit-position caps as [vix_below, cap] pairs, first match wins — config home for the hardcoded '6 if vix<20 else 4 if vix<25 else 2' in manager.py (register CD item). max_credit_positions stays the absolute ceiling. |
| `risk.max_symbol_concentration_pct` | `float` | 0.05 - 0.5 | 0.2 | 0.2 | config.yaml | Maximum fraction of the account in one symbol (a risk-manager gate separate from the aggregate cap `positions.max_portfolio_risk_pct`). |
| `risk.iv_rank_cap` | `float` | 0.0 - 100.0 | 85.0 | 85 | config.yaml | Config home for AIT_IV_RANK_CAP — no new short premium above this IV rank. |
| `risk.max_positions_per_expiry` | `int` | 1 - 20 | 3 | 3 | config.yaml | Config home for AIT_MAX_PER_EXPIRY — positions sharing one expiry stack pin/gamma risk into a single settlement date. |
| `risk.skip_macro_events` | `bool` | - | true | true | config.yaml | Macro-event protection (entry gates + rule-3d flatten for undefined-risk shapes). |
| `risk.credit_vix_halt` | `float` | 15.0 - 60.0 | 28.0 | 28 | config.yaml | No NEW credit entries when VIX is at/above this level — cheap vol-regime brake for short-premium strategies. |
| `risk.weekend_gap_cutoff_et` | `str` | - | 14:30 | 14:30 | config.yaml | From this ET time on a Friday, weekend_gap_strategies need weekend_gap_min_confidence to be entered (weekend gap risk for undefined-risk shorts). |
| `risk.weekend_gap_min_confidence` | `float` | 0.5 - 0.99 | 0.9 | 0.9 | config.yaml | Confidence a weekend_gap_strategies entry needs after weekend_gap_cutoff_et on Friday. |
| `risk.weekend_gap_strategies` | `list[str]` | - | [short_strangle] | [short_strangle] | config.yaml | Strategies subject to the Friday-afternoon confidence rule. |

| `ml.vol_magnitude_threshold_pct` | `float` | 0.0 - 0.5 | 0.07 | 0.07 | config.yaml | The vol-magnitude model's 'big move' size (a +/- fraction); bigger than the range band on purpose. |
| `ml.vol_magnitude_horizon_days` | `int` | 1 - 120 | 30 | 30 | config.yaml | Days ahead the vol-magnitude model looks for that move. |
| `ml.vol_magnitude_min_edge_over_baseline` | `float` | 0.0 - 1.0 | 0.1 | 0.1 | config.yaml | The vol-magnitude model is only used when its CV edge over the baseline is at least this. |
| `ml.direction_label_threshold_pct` | `float` | 0.0 - 0.2 | 0.01 | 0.01 | config.yaml | The direction model's 3-class label: a forward return above +this is bullish, below -this bearish, otherwise neutral. |
| `ml.direction_label_horizon_days` | `int` | 1 - 60 | 5 | 5 | config.yaml | Days forward over which the direction label is measured (also the rows dropped from the end of the training set). |
| `ml.direction_cv_splits` | `int` | 2 - 20 | 5 | 5 | config.yaml | Walk-forward validation folds of the direction model (and of the retrain's hyperparameter search). |
| `ml.direction_cv_gap_days` | `int` | 0 - 60 | 5 | 5 | config.yaml | Purge gap between the direction model's training and validation rows. |
| `ml.cv_min_val_rows` | `int` | 5 - 500 | 20 | 20 | config.yaml | Smallest validation fold of the direction model's walk-forward split. |
| `ml.cv_min_train_rows` | `int` | 10 - 2000 | 50 | 50 | config.yaml | A direction-model fold whose training part is shorter than this is skipped (with fewer than two usable folds the split falls back to sklearn's TimeSeriesSplit). |
| `ml.binary_cv_splits` | `int` | 2 - 20 | 4 | 4 | config.yaml | Walk-forward folds of the two binary models (range, vol-magnitude). |
| `ml.binary_cv_min_gap_days` | `int` | 0 - 60 | 5 | 5 | config.yaml | Minimum purge gap in the binary models' validation; the gap used is the larger of this and the label horizon, so overlapping labels cannot leak into the validation score. |
| `ml.label_balance_min` | `float` | 0.0 - 0.5 | 0.05 | 0.05 | config.yaml | A binary label whose positive rate is below this is warned about (too few positives to learn from). |
| `ml.label_balance_max` | `float` | 0.5 - 1.0 | 0.98 | 0.98 | config.yaml | A binary label whose positive rate is above this (almost always positive) is also warned about. Warning only. |
| `ml.min_class_samples` | `int` | 2 - 1000 | 10 | 10 | config.yaml | A binary model is not trained unless each class has at least this many rows. |
| `ml.retrain_optuna_trials` | `int` | 1 - 2000 | 50 | 50 | config.yaml | Optuna trials of the live retrain's optional hyperparameter search. |
| `ml.retrain_optuna_seed` | `int` | 0 - 2147483647 | 42 | 42 | config.yaml | Seed of that search's TPE sampler. |
| `ml.rollback_margin` | `float` | 0.0 - 0.5 | 0.05 | 0.05 | config.yaml | A retrained direction model whose average CV accuracy is more than this below the previous one's (5 percentage points) is rolled back. |
| `ml.observe_mode_neutral_confidence` | `float` | 0.5 - 0.9 | 0.6 | 0.6 | config.yaml | Observe mode only: the confidence a direction-neutral structure carries into risk validation instead of the directional confidence. |
| `ml.regime_override_confidence` | `float` | 0.5 - 0.99 | 0.8 | 0.8 | config.yaml | A HIGH_VOLATILITY regime classification at or above this confidence overrides the ML direction to NEUTRAL at entry. |
| `ml.drift_detection_enabled` | `bool` | - | false | false | config.yaml | Master switch of the live drift detector. |
| `ml.drift_window_size` | `int` | 20 - 500 | 50 | 50 | config.yaml | N = how many of the most recent RESOLVED predictions (a prediction whose trade has closed) the detector looks at. |
| `ml.drift_accuracy_threshold` | `float` | 0.2 - 0.8 | 0.4 | 0.4 | config.yaml | If the share of those predictions that were right falls below this, the model is flagged as drifting and an early retrain is requested. 0.40 = right less than 40% of the time; a 3-way direction call guessing at random is right about 33%, so this is only just above chance. |
| `ml.drift_high_confidence` | `float` | 0.6 - 0.99 | 0.8 | 0.8 | config.yaml | Predictions made with at least this confidence form the 'high-confidence group', which should be right about this often (80% confident should mean about 80% right). |
| `ml.drift_calibration_threshold` | `float` | 0.05 - 0.6 | 0.25 | 0.25 | config.yaml | If the high-confidence group is right LESS often than drift_high_confidence by more than this (0.25 = 25 percentage points, i.e. it is right under 55% of the time at the defaults), the model is overconfident and is flagged as drifting. |
| `ml.drift_min_samples` | `int` | 5 - 500 | 20 | 20 | config.yaml | Nothing is reported until at least this many predictions in the window have an outcome. |
| `ml.drift_min_high_confidence_samples` | `int` | 1 - 500 | 5 | 5 | config.yaml | The calibration test needs at least this many resolved high-confidence predictions; with fewer it is skipped and only accuracy counts. |
| `ml.drift_check_interval` | `int` | 1 - 500 | 10 | 10 | config.yaml | The full check runs at most once per this many newly recorded predictions; in between, the last report is returned. |
| `ml.model_versions_kept` | `int` | 1 - 100 | 5 | 5 | config.yaml | How many saved direction-model versions are kept on disk; older ones are deleted each time a model is saved. |

## Regime classifier (`regime`)

| Setting | Type | Allowed range | Default | Shipped | Listed in | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `regime.high_vol_vix` | `float` | 15.0 - 80.0 | 30.0 | 30 | config.yaml | VIX above this classifies HIGH_VOLATILITY. |
| `regime.high_vol_realized` | `float` | 0.15 - 2.0 | 0.4 | 0.4 | config.yaml | Annualised realised vol above this classifies HIGH_VOLATILITY (either trigger is enough). |
| `regime.iv_crush_iv_rank_max` | `float` | 0.0 - 1.0 | 0.25 | 0.25 | config.yaml | IV_CRUSH needs IV rank (0-1) below this, realised vol below `iv_crush_vol_max` and \|trend strength\| below `iv_crush_trend_max`. |
| `regime.iv_crush_vol_max` | `float` | 0.01 - 1.0 | 0.2 | 0.2 | config.yaml | Realised-vol ceiling of IV_CRUSH. |
| `regime.iv_crush_trend_max` | `float` | 0.0 - 1.0 | 0.2 | 0.2 | config.yaml | \|Trend strength\| ceiling of IV_CRUSH. |
| `regime.mean_revert_hurst_max` | `float` | 0.0 - 0.5 | 0.4 | 0.4 | config.yaml | MEAN_REVERTING needs the Hurst exponent below this and \|trend strength\| below `mean_revert_trend_max`. |
| `regime.mean_revert_trend_max` | `float` | 0.0 - 1.0 | 0.25 | 0.25 | config.yaml | \|Trend strength\| ceiling of MEAN_REVERTING. |
| `regime.low_vol_vix` | `float` | 5.0 - 30.0 | 15.0 | 15 | config.yaml | VIX below this (or realised vol below low_vol_realized) is the LOW_VOLATILITY branch. |
| `regime.low_vol_realized` | `float` | 0.02 - 0.6 | 0.12 | 0.12 | config.yaml | Realised vol below this is the LOW_VOLATILITY branch. |
| `regime.low_vol_trend_breakout` | `float` | 0.05 - 1.0 | 0.3 | 0.3 | config.yaml | Inside the low-vol branch, \|trend\| above this is TRENDING_UP/DOWN instead of LOW_VOLATILITY. |
| `regime.strong_trend` | `float` | 0.05 - 1.0 | 0.35 | 0.35 | config.yaml | \|trend strength\| above this (outside the branches above) classifies TRENDING_UP/DOWN. |
| `regime.trend_sma_periods` | `list[int]` | - | [10, 20, 50] | [10, 20, 50] | config.yaml | The trend score averages the slope of the simple moving average of each of these lengths (days). |
| `regime.trend_slope_lookback` | `int` | 1 - 60 | 5 | 5 | config.yaml | A moving average's slope is its percentage change over this many days. |
| `regime.trend_slope_scale` | `float` | 0.0 - 10000.0 | 100.0 | 100.0 | config.yaml | That slope is multiplied by this and clamped to [-1, 1] (100 means a 1% move in 5 days scores 1.0). |
| `regime.trend_deviation_periods` | `list[int]` | - | [20, 50] | [20, 50] | config.yaml | The trend score also averages how far the price sits above or below the moving average of each of these lengths (days). |
| `regime.trend_deviation_scale` | `float` | 0.0 - 10000.0 | 10.0 | 10.0 | config.yaml | That distance, as a fraction of the average, is multiplied by this and clamped to [-1, 1] (10 means 10% away scores 1.0). |
| `regime.trend_momentum_days` | `int` | 1 - 252 | 20 | 20 | config.yaml | The trend score also includes the price return over this many days. |
| `regime.trend_momentum_scale` | `float` | 0.0 - 10000.0 | 5.0 | 5.0 | config.yaml | That return is multiplied by this and clamped to [-1, 1] (5 means a 20% return scores 1.0). |
| `regime.high_vol_confidence_floor` | `float` | 0.5 - 1.0 | 0.8 | 0.8 | config.yaml | A HIGH_VOLATILITY classification reports a confidence of at least this. |
| `regime.high_vol_confidence_cap` | `float` | 0.5 - 1.0 | 0.9 | 0.9 | config.yaml | At most this confidence is reported for HIGH_VOLATILITY. |
| `regime.high_vol_confidence_vol_scale` | `float` | 0.0 - 5.0 | 0.5 | 0.5 | config.yaml | Between the floor and the cap the confidence is realized volatility divided by this (0.40 vol -> 0.80). |
| `regime.iv_crush_confidence` | `float` | 0.0 - 1.0 | 0.7 | 0.7 | config.yaml | The confidence an IV_CRUSH classification reports (reported only: no live rule compares against it). |
| `regime.mean_revert_confidence_floor` | `float` | 0.0 - 1.0 | 0.6 | 0.6 | config.yaml | A MEAN_REVERTING classification reports max(this, 1 - Hurst exponent) (reported only). |
| `regime.low_vol_confidence` | `float` | 0.0 - 1.0 | 0.7 | 0.7 | config.yaml | The confidence a LOW_VOLATILITY classification reports (reported only). |
| `regime.trend_confidence_cap` | `float` | 0.5 - 1.0 | 0.95 | 0.95 | config.yaml | A TRENDING_UP / TRENDING_DOWN classification reports min(this, \|trend strength\|) (reported only). |
| `regime.range_confidence_floor` | `float` | 0.0 - 1.0 | 0.5 | 0.5 | config.yaml | A RANGE_BOUND classification reports max(this, 1 - 2 x \|trend strength\|) (reported only). |
| `regime.min_history_rows` | `int` | 21 - 1000 | 60 | 60 | config.yaml | The classifier needs at least this many daily bars; with fewer it returns RANGE_BOUND at confidence 0 (it makes no call). |
| `regime.iv_rank_min_rows` | `int` | 2 - 1000 | 60 | 60 | config.yaml | The IV-rank proxy (today's 20-day realized vol as a percentile of its own recent range) is computed only from at least this many 20-day-vol values, else it reports a neutral 0.5. |
| `regime.iv_rank_window_rows` | `int` | 2 - 2000 | 252 | 252 | config.yaml | The IV-rank proxy compares today's 20-day vol with the highest and lowest 20-day vol over the last this many values (252 = one trading year; fewer are used while the history is shorter). |

| Setting | Type | Allowed range | Default | Shipped | Listed in | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| `meta_label.min_probability` | `float` | 0.3 - 0.8 | 0.5 | 0.5 | config.yaml | Minimum predicted probability of profit for the meta-labeler to let a trade through, when it acts. |
| `meta_label.retrain_with_primary` | `bool` | - | true | true | config.yaml | Not read by any code: the live trainer has no meta-labeler retrain, and the gate itself is off. |
| `meta_label.min_trades_for_training` | `int` | 10 - 1000 | 30 | 30 | config.yaml | The meta-labeler is not trained on fewer closed trades than this. min_closes_to_enable below is the separate question of when its output is TRUSTED for live entries. |
| `meta_label.min_class_trades` | `int` | 2 - 500 | 5 | 5 | config.yaml | The meta-labeler also needs at least this many profitable and this many unprofitable closed trades. |
| `meta_label.cv_max_splits` | `int` | 2 - 20 | 5 | 5 | config.yaml | Its training cross-validation uses at most this many folds. |
| `meta_label.cv_min_rows_per_split` | `int` | 2 - 500 | 10 | 10 | config.yaml | One fold per this many rows, never fewer than 2. |
| `meta_label.min_feature_coverage` | `int` | 1 - 20 | 15 | 15 | config.yaml | Of the 20 meta-label inputs, at least this many must carry real (non-constant) data before a freshly trained model is armed. |
| `meta_label.max_artifact_age_days` | `int` | 1 - 3650 | 45 | 45 | config.yaml | A saved meta-label model older than this is stale and refused at load. |
| `meta_label.min_closes_to_enable` | `int` | 30 - 500 | 100 | 100 | config.yaml | Real, verdict-eligible closed trades (the same population reporting.go_live.real_close_count/the go-live scorecard grades) required before the meta-label gate is trusted for LIVE entries -- regardless of `enabled` above or whether a model has already trained. |

## Assignment response (`assignment_response`)

| Setting | Type | Allowed range | Default | Shipped | Listed in | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assignment_response.policy` | `Literal['close_only', 'roll_only', 'close_or_roll']` | - | close_only | close_only | config.yaml | Close_only: today's behavior, always close an at-risk leg. roll_only/close_or_roll: rule 3/3e report a roll candidate (PositionStatus.roll_side) instead of closing outright, but execute_rolls below is ADDITIONALLY required before anything is actually compared or placed -- same two-layer gate condor_defense.enabled/execute_rolls already uses. |
| `assignment_response.execute_rolls` | `bool` | - | false | false | config.yaml | A SEPARATE opt-in from policy above, mirroring CondorDefenseConfig.execute_rolls exactly. policy != 'close_only' alone still only makes rule 3/3e REPORT a roll candidate -- execute_rolls=True is additionally required before the orchestrator ever runs the close-or-roll comparison or places a real order. |
| `assignment_response.comparison_model` | `Literal['heuristic', 'ev']` | - | heuristic | heuristic | config.yaml | Which model decides close-vs-roll once policy == 'close_or_roll' AND execute_rolls is True. 'heuristic': the cheap credit/max-loss proxy (execution/roll_comparison.py, heuristic_should_roll). 'ev': prices both sides at each leg's own model-implied fair value instead of raw market quotes (ev_should_roll) -- more precise in principle, but has NOT been backtested: the historical per-strike vol-surface backfill this nee… |
| `assignment_response.max_rolls_per_position` | `int` | 0 - 10 | 2 | 2 | config.yaml | Hard cap on how many times ONE position may be rolled (walks rolled_from_trade_id via state.py's count_roll_ancestors), enforced once in orchestrator._execute_roll regardless of which system triggered the roll. |
| `assignment_response.roll_target_dte_min` | `int` | 1 - 90 | 14 | 14 | config.yaml | Floor of the later-expiry search window for a roll target. |
| `assignment_response.roll_target_dte_max` | `int` | 2 - 120 | 30 | 30 | config.yaml | Ceiling of the later-expiry search window for a roll target. |
| `assignment_response.roll_min_credit` | `float` | 0.0 - 5.0 | 0.2 | 0.2 | config.yaml | Refuse a roll whose net credit (old vertical bought back, new vertical sold) is below this. |
| `assignment_response.roll_short_delta_target` | `float` | 0.05 - 0.5 | 0.2 | 0.2 | config.yaml | Target \|delta\| of the NEW short strike when a roll re-establishes the at-risk vertical. |
| `assignment_response.roll_short_delta_tolerance` | `float` | 0.01 - 0.25 | 0.07 | 0.07 | config.yaml | How far the nearest liquid strike's \|delta\| may sit from roll_short_delta_target before the roll is refused (select_roll_target returns None). 0.07 matches Strategy._find_strike_by_delta's default tolerance. |

## Condor defense (staged) (`condor_defense`)

| Setting | Type | Allowed range | Default | Shipped | Listed in | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `condor_defense.enabled` | `bool` | - | false | false | config.yaml | Off: check_positions never consults this config (once a future wave wires it in) — always hold. |
| `condor_defense.side` | `Literal['tested_only', 'untested_only', 'both']` | - | untested_only | untested_only | config.yaml | Which rolls are allowed. tested_only: only roll the side under pressure (a debit, buys distance). untested_only: only roll the side NOT under pressure (a credit, widens the aggregate breakeven — the playbook's primary recommendation). both: either, per the table. |
| `condor_defense.monitor_delta_max` | `float` | 0.0 - 1.0 | 0.25 | 0.25 | config.yaml | Below this, the tested short is not under enough pressure to act on — hold. |
| `condor_defense.roll_untested_delta_min` | `float` | 0.0 - 1.0 | 0.25 | 0.25 | config.yaml | Floor of the tested-short delta band (inclusive) that triggers rolling the UNTESTED side for a credit. |
| `condor_defense.roll_untested_delta_max` | `float` | 0.0 - 1.0 | 0.3 | 0.3 | config.yaml | Ceiling of the roll-untested delta band (exclusive — at this delta the tested-side row below takes over). |
| `condor_defense.roll_untested_dte_min` | `int` | 1 - 365 | 14 | 14 | config.yaml | Floor (inclusive) of the DTE window the roll-untested row applies in. |
| `condor_defense.roll_untested_dte_max` | `int` | 1 - 365 | 21 | 21 | config.yaml | Ceiling (inclusive) of the DTE window the roll-untested row applies in — beyond this the tested-side row takes over. |
| `condor_defense.roll_tested_delta_min` | `float` | 0.0 - 1.0 | 0.3 | 0.3 | config.yaml | Floor (inclusive) of the tested-short delta band that triggers rolling the TESTED side itself for a debit, when DTE is also >= roll_tested_dte_min. |
| `condor_defense.roll_tested_dte_min` | `int` | 1 - 365 | 22 | 22 | config.yaml | Floor (inclusive) of the DTE window the roll-tested row applies in — explicit (not just "not in the roll-untested window") so the two bands can't silently overlap if either is retuned independently. |
| `condor_defense.close_delta_threshold` | `float` | 0.0 - 1.0 | 0.4 | 0.4 | config.yaml | At or above this delta, close outright regardless of DTE or side setting — high-gamma / near-expiry, the document's table row 4. |
| `condor_defense.execute_rolls` | `bool` | - | false | false | config.yaml | A SEPARATE opt-in from `enabled` above. enabled=True alone still only makes CLOSE actionable and reports a ROLL verdict (action=ROLL) without acting on it — execute_rolls=True is additionally required before orchestrator._execute_roll ever selects a target, prepares a combo, or places a real order. |

## Exit rules (`exit`)

| Setting | Type | Allowed range | Default | Shipped | Listed in | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `exit.exit_cross_amount` | `float` | 0.01 - 0.5 | 0.1 | 0.1 | config.yaml | How far a combo exit limit crosses the spread so the close actually fills. |
| `exit.exit_mark_multiple` | `float` | 1.05 - 3.0 | 1.5 | 1.5 | config.yaml | Ceiling on a credit buyback as a multiple of the CURRENT marked cost to close. |
| `exit.exit_min_ceiling_headroom` | `float` | 0.1 - 2.0 | 0.6 | 0.6 | config.yaml | The least absolute headroom the mark-anchored ceiling leaves above the mark. |
| `exit.exit_band_ttl_seconds` | `float` | 30.0 - 3600.0 | 300.0 | 300 | config.yaml | How long a broker-stated price band caps later exit attempts. |
| `exit.exit_unfilled_escalation_pct` | `float` | 0.0 - 0.25 | 0.05 | 0.05 | config.yaml | Each consecutive QUOTED exit placement that did not fill raises the next limit by this fraction of the marketable price (n-th retry: x(1 + pct*n)), under the same caps (wing width, mark-anchored ceiling, broker band). |
| `exit.exit_reprice_step` | `float` | 0.01 - 1.0 | 0.1 | 0.1 | config.yaml | How far each consecutive NO-QUOTE exit placement steps above the last (anchor + cross + n*step, capped). re-placed the identical price every backoff. |
| `exit.exit_pending_rest_seconds` | `float` | 30.0 - 1800.0 | 300.0 | 300 | config.yaml | How long a working, unfilled close order rests before check_fills cancels it so the monitor can re-trigger the exit. |
| `exit.exit_stop_pending_rest_seconds` | `float` | 15.0 - 1800.0 | 120.0 | 120 | config.yaml | How long an unfilled stop exit (stop loss, short-strike touch, trailing stop, breakeven stop) or an exit that must get out (condor defense close, assignment risk, expiry at 0 or 1 days) rests before a cancel is requested; shorter than the rest for ordinary exits so it re-prices sooner. |
| `exit.exit_blind_credit_multiple` | `float` | 1.0 - 5.0 | 2.0 | 2.0 | config.yaml | With no quote and no fresh mark, the most a credit buyback may pay is this multiple of the entry credit (and never more than the wing width). priced that state at the raw width — the structural max loss. |
| `exit.exit_intrinsic_floor_enabled` | `bool` | - | true | true | config.yaml | A condor close is never offered for less than the structure is worth at the underlying: its intrinsic value plus `exit_cross_amount`, never above the wing width. |
| `exit.exit_near_expiry_dte` | `int` | 0 - 5 | 1 | 1 | config.yaml | Days to expiry at or below which a credit close that must get out (a stop, the short-strike touch, assignment risk, condor defense, the expiry exit; not a take-profit) may be offered up to the wing width (the most it can ever cost) and the intrinsic floor allows for a delayed spot (`exit_intrinsic_delayed_band_pct`). |
| `exit.exit_intrinsic_delayed_band_pct` | `float` | 0.0 - 0.02 | 0.0025 | 0.0025 | config.yaml | Near expiry on delayed market data, the intrinsic floor is the worst case over the spot plus or minus this fraction (delayed quotes are about 15 minutes old; 0.25% is about one standard deviation of that move at 20% implied volatility). 0 uses the spot as given. |
| `exit.credit_touch_stop` | `bool` | - | true | true | config.yaml | Config home for AIT_CREDIT_TOUCH_STOP — close a credit structure when the underlying touches a short strike. |
| `exit.trailing_stop_pct` | `float` | 0.1 - 0.5 | 0.25 | 0.25 | config.yaml | Trailing stop distance below the high-water mark, as a fraction of cost (debit structures; credit structures use the short-strike touch exit). |
| `exit.breakeven_trigger_pct` | `float` | 0.1 - 0.8 | 0.3 | 0.3 | config.yaml | Profit, as a fraction of cost, at which the stop moves to breakeven (debit structures). |
| `exit.partial_exit_levels` | `list[dict]` | - | [{pnl_pct: 0.5, close_pct: 0.33}, {pnl_pct: 1.0, close_pct: 0.33}] | [{pnl_pct: 0.5, close_pct: 0.33}, {pnl_pct: 1.0, close_pct: 0.33}] | config.yaml | Scale-out milestones: at each pnl_pct the position closes close_pct of itself, once per level (strategies that use them). |
| `exit.time_decay_scaling` | `bool` | - | true | true | config.yaml | Shrinks the take-profit target as expiry nears (the take-profit ladder). |
| `exit.volatility_adjusted_stops` | `bool` | - | true | true | config.yaml | Widens the stop for volatile underlyings (debit structures only). |
| `exit.initial_stop_loss_pct` | `float` | 0.15 - 0.75 | 0.5 | 0.5 | config.yaml | Fixed stop, as a fraction of cost, before the breakeven trigger activates (debit structures). |
| `exit.auto_hedge` | `bool` | - | false | false | config.yaml | Not read by any code: no hedging code exists in the live tree. |
| `exit.max_quote_staleness_seconds` | `float` | 30.0 - 900.0 | 180.0 | 180.0 | neither (schema default) | Underlying quote older than this (by exchange tick time) marks the touch stop's input DEGRADED — it then needs two agreeing ticks to fire instead of one. |
| `exit.touch_confirm_ticks` | `int` | 1 - 5 | 2 | 2 | neither (schema default) | Consecutive agreeing evaluations required before a touch stop fires on a degraded/frozen quote. 1 = fire on a single stale print. |
| `exit.max_quote_spread_pct` | `float` | 0.02 - 0.5 | 0.15 | 0.15 | neither (schema default) | Underlying quote bid-ask spread above this marks the touch stop's input DEGRADED — same two-agreeing-ticks confirmation as a stale or outlier print. |
| `exit.max_quote_jump_pct` | `float` | 0.02 - 0.5 | 0.1 | 0.1 | neither (schema default) | A move in the underlying quote, against the last confirmed price, above this marks the touch stop's input as degraded (it then waits for corroborating ticks). |
| `exit.thesis_direction_flip_confidence` | `float` | 0.5 - 0.99 | 0.7 | 0.7 | config.yaml | The open-position thesis check exits when the ML direction has flipped against the entry direction with confidence above this. |
| `exit.thesis_regime_shift_confidence` | `float` | 0.5 - 0.99 | 0.7 | 0.7 | config.yaml | The thesis check treats a regime shift (trending -> high volatility) as invalidating only when the regime classification confidence is above this. |
| `exit.thesis_vix_spike_pct` | `float` | 0.05 - 2.0 | 0.3 | 0.3 | config.yaml | The thesis check exits when VIX has risen more than this fraction since entry (0.30 = +30%). |
| `exit.order_visibility_grace_seconds` | `float` | 5.0 - 60.0 | 10.0 | 10 | config.yaml | A freshly placed EXIT order is ignored by the fill checker while younger than this, so it has time to appear in IBKR's trade list (a brand-new order would otherwise read as cancelled). |
| `exit.foreign_exit_escalation_seconds` | `float` | 60.0 - 3600.0 | 300.0 | 300 | config.yaml | An exit order that belongs to ANOTHER clientId cannot be cancelled from this session, so once it has been working this long the executor pages the operator instead of looping on a cancel that cannot land. |
| `exit.zombie_exit_revert_seconds` | `float` | 120.0 - 7200.0 | 900.0 | 900 | config.yaml | The zombie cap. |

| `sizing_probe.dte` | `int` | 1 - 365 | 21 | 21 | config.yaml | Probe days to expiry — the builder's own fallback DTE. |
| `sizing_probe.strike_grids` | `list[float]` | - | [1.0, 5.0] | [1.0, 5.0] | config.yaml | Strike spacings to probe, in dollars. |
| `sizing_probe.iv_rank` | `float` | 0.0 - 100.0 | 55.0 | 55.0 | config.yaml | IV rank handed to the builder. |

## Scheduled data collection (`data_collection`)

| Setting | Type | Allowed range | Default | Shipped | Listed in | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data_collection.short_dte_enabled` | `bool` | - | false | false | neither (schema default) | Run the 0-6 DTE friction collector from the supervisor on weekdays. |
| `data_collection.short_dte_time_et` | `str` | - | 15:30 | 15:30 | neither (schema default) | ET wall-clock time of the daily run, HH:MM. It must fall inside the session: after the close IB no longer serves that day's expiring contracts, so a later run cannot capture 0 DTE. |
| `data_collection.short_dte_symbols` | `list[str]` | - | [QQQ] | [QQQ] | neither (schema default) | Underlyings to collect. |
| `data_collection.short_dte_client_id` | `int` | 1 - 999999 | 91 | 91 | neither (schema default) | IB API client id for the collector. |
| `data_collection.short_dte_max_dte` | `int` | 1 - 14 | 6 | 6 | neither (schema default) | Furthest expiry (days) to sample. 6 matches the friction bands (0-2, 3-6). |
| `data_collection.short_dte_duration` | `str` | - | 7 D | 7 D | neither (schema default) | History requested per contract. |
| `data_collection.lifecycle` | `bool` | - | false | false | neither (schema default) | Capture each contract's LIFE instead of 'every contract <= short_dte_max_dte, every day'. Stage A = expiring today..+lifecycle_expiring_days (the perishable part, DTE 0 first); stage B = far-listed expiries at 15-21 DTE whose DTE 31-45 tail is not stored, capped per run. |
| `data_collection.lifecycle_duration` | `str` | - | 30 D | 30 D | neither (schema default) | History requested per contract in lifecycle mode. 30 D is what IB serves for hourly BID/ASK bars of a listed option. |
| `data_collection.lifecycle_expiring_days` | `int` | 0 - 5 | 1 | 1 | neither (schema default) | Stage A covers expiries today..today+N. 1 (default) means every contract is requested on its last day AND the day before, so one missed day costs at most that day's bars. |
| `data_collection.lifecycle_thin_every` | `int` | 1 - 10 | 5 | 5 | neither (schema default) | Plan strikes from every Nth session of the underlying's path. |
| `data_collection.lifecycle_incremental_sessions` | `int` | 1 - 10 | 3 | 3 | neither (schema default) | An expiry captured before (typically the day before) is planned over its newest N sessions only, unthinned: its last day adds little else, so the second capture costs about a third of the first. |
| `data_collection.lifecycle_max_far_contracts` | `int` | 0 - 400 | 120 | 120 | neither (schema default) | Stage-B contract cap per run (120 is about 43 minutes at IB's pacing); the first owed expiry is always taken so a backlog drains, the rest is deferred to the next run. |
| `data_collection.short_dte_timeout_minutes` | `int` | 10 - 600 | 150 | 150 | neither (schema default) | Hard wall-clock cap for one run; the job kills the process after this. |
| `data_collection.short_dte_idle_minutes` | `int` | 2 - 120 | 20 | 20 | neither (schema default) | Kill the run if it prints nothing for this long (progress is printed every 10 contracts, about 3.6 minutes apart, so silence means a hang). |
